task.title:
You are the lead engineer on "T-24", a tool for the IBM Bob 2.0 hackathon (theme: improve a developer workflow). Tagline: "Prove whether you're affected before the CRA clock runs out." Plan the whole project before any code. Output a plan, then create ONLY these files: AGENTS.md, README.md (overwrite the skeleton), .bobignore, docs/PLAN.md, docs/DATA_CONTRACT.md.

PROBLEM: Since 11 Sep 2026 the EU Cyber Resilience Act (Article 14) requires manufacturers to send ENISA an early warning within 24h of becoming aware of an actively exploited vulnerability in their product, a notification within 72h, and a final report within 14 days. Fines reach EUR 15M or 2.5% of worldwide turnover. When a dependency advisory drops, developers spend hours answering "are we even affected?" by grepping, reading advisories and arguing. Most alerts are for code paths the product never calls.

SOLUTION: a Python 3.11 CLI + Bob custom mode + Bob skill that, given a product repo and a set of security advisories:
 1. Advisory reader (LLM): extracts package, affected version range, fixed version, vulnerable symbols (functions/classes/filters named in the advisory), and preconditions. Every extracted symbol MUST appear verbatim in the advisory text, otherwise it is dropped (deterministic check).
 2. Inventory (deterministic): resolves installed versions from requirements.txt and checks them against the range with packaging.specifiers.
 3. Reachability (deterministic): builds a Python AST import+call graph from declared entry points, handles aliasing (import x as y, from x import f as g, attribute chains), and returns the evidence path file:line -> ... -> vulnerable symbol.
 4. Verdict engine (deterministic, the LLM NEVER sets it). OpenVEX statuses:
    - version not in range -> not_affected / vulnerable_code_not_present
    - in range + symbol reachable -> affected (with evidence path)
    - in range + symbols named + none reachable + 100% of project files parsed -> not_affected / vulnerable_code_not_in_execute_path
    - anything else (no symbols named, parse failures, preconditions like proxy config that static analysis cannot prove) -> under_investigation
 5. CRA clock: if a finding is affected AND the user marks it actively exploited with an awareness timestamp, compute the 24h / 72h / 14d deadlines and draft the ENISA early warning and notification (markdown, fields per CRA Art. 14). Otherwise explain why no report is due.
 6. Outputs: OpenVEX 0.2.0 JSON (out/vex.json), out/dossier.json (exact shape below), out/drafts/*.md.
 7. LLM provider: IBM watsonx.ai Granite via env vars (WATSONX_APIKEY, WATSONX_PROJECT_ID, WATSONX_URL); fallback Fireworks (FIREWORKS_API_KEY). Extractions are cached to cache/ so the demo runs fully offline with NO keys.

DEMO PRODUCT (under demo_product/): a tiny Flask "label printer" service pinned to real old versions with real public advisories:
 - PyYAML 5.3.1, CVE-2020-14343 (full_load / FullLoader arbitrary code execution). The app calls yaml.full_load on uploaded config => expected AFFECTED
 - Pillow 9.5.0, CVE-2023-50447 (PIL.ImageMath.eval code execution). The app makes thumbnails but never uses ImageMath => expected NOT_AFFECTED (not in execute path)
 - Jinja2 3.1.2, CVE-2024-22195 (xmlattr filter XSS). The app renders templates but never uses xmlattr => expected NOT_AFFECTED
 - requests 2.30.0, CVE-2023-32681 (Proxy-Authorization leak on redirect when proxies are configured). Precondition not provable statically => expected UNDER_INVESTIGATION
Verify each CVE id, affected range, fixed version and vulnerable symbol against the GitHub Advisory Database before relying on it; if any fact above is wrong, correct it and tell me. Advisory texts go in advisories/ as markdown with a SOURCE URL line (GitHub Advisory Database, CC-BY-4.0). Keep docs/DATA_SOURCES.md listing every website used.

TEAM SPLIT: I own t24/, demo_product/, advisories/, tests/, cache/, .bob/. My teammate owns dossier/ and vercel.json and builds the web page in parallel. Never create or edit files under dossier/.

AGENTS.md must include these rules: the verdict is deterministic and the LLM never sets or overrides it; never claim not_affected without a complete parse; every claim in a draft report cites a file:line or an advisory line; tests before implementation for each module; no network calls in tests; modules under 300 lines; never edit dossier/; out/dossier.json must follow docs/DATA_CONTRACT.md exactly.

DATA CONTRACT: write docs/DATA_CONTRACT.md containing exactly this example and these field rules.
{
  "product": "demo_product",
  "scanned_at": "2026-09-27T02:00:00Z",
  "duration_s": 3.2,
  "summary": {"advisories": 4, "affected": 1, "not_affected": 2, "under_investigation": 1, "emergency_releases_avoided": 2},
  "clock": {
    "cve": "CVE-2020-14343",
    "aware_at": "2026-09-27T02:00:00Z",
    "early_warning_due": "2026-09-28T02:00:00Z",
    "notification_due": "2026-09-30T02:00:00Z",
    "final_report_due": "2026-10-11T02:00:00Z"
  },
  "findings": [
    {
      "cve": "CVE-2020-14343",
      "package": "PyYAML",
      "installed": "5.3.1",
      "affected_range": "<5.4",
      "fixed_version": "5.4",
      "symbols": ["full_load"],
      "status": "affected",
      "justification": null,
      "evidence": [
        {"file": "demo_product/app.py", "line": 18, "function": "upload_config", "call": "yaml.full_load"}
      ],
      "reason": "full_load is reachable from route /upload-config",
      "advisory_source": "https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8q59-q68h-6hv4",
      "drafts": ["out/drafts/early_warning_CVE-2020-14343.md", "out/drafts/notification_CVE-2020-14343.md"]
    }
  ],
  "coverage": {"files_found": 3, "files_parsed": 3},
  "vex_path": "out/vex.json"
}
Field rules: status is one of affected | not_affected | under_investigation | fixed. justification is an OpenVEX justification string when status is not_affected, else null. evidence is the ordered hop list from entry point to vulnerable call, [] when none. clock is null when no finding is both affected and actively exploited. drafts is [] when no report is due.

Plan the module layout (t24/advisory.py, inventory.py, reach.py, verdict.py, clock.py, vex.py, report.py, cli.py, __main__.py), the test plan (pytest, fixtures from demo_product), and the order of work. Keep scope to what one person can build in about 10 hours.

task.description: Verify CVE facts and cross-check advisory data
Write docs/PLAN.md
Write docs/DATA_CONTRACT.md
Write AGENTS.md
Write README.md
Fix docs/PLAN.md: update advisory facts table, remove correction note, add Decisions section
Add advisory facts rule to AGENTS.md
Fetch GHSA records via curl and build advisories/*.md + docs/DATA_SOURCES.md
Build demo_product/ (app.py, config.py, templates/label.html, requirements.txt)
Build t24/__init__.py, t24/inventory.py, tests/test_inventory.py
Create pyproject.toml, .gitignore, .bobignore
Create .venv, install deps, run pytest, fix until green
Show pytest output and repo tree
FIX 1: Regenerate advisory files with published text only; save raw JSON; move expected answers to tests/fixtures/expected_extractions.json; update AGENTS.md
FIX 2: Tri-state VersionCheck (present flag, in_range bool|None); update tests
CORE reach.py: implement reach_imports.py, reach_graph.py, tests first
Run pytest until all green
Run reach against demo_product and print results
Read current reach implementation files
Write adversarial fixture projects + tests/test_reach_adversarial.py (tests first, watch fail)
Fix reach modules to handle all adversarial cases; add uncertain field to ReachResult
Add soundness rule to AGENTS.md
Write docs/REACHABILITY.md
Run full suite until green; run demo_product scan; verify unchanged demo output

<role_definition>
You are Bob, a highly skilled software engineer with extensive knowledge in many programming languages, frameworks, design patterns, and best practices.
</role_definition>

<investigate_before_answering>
Never speculate about code you have not opened. If the user references a specific file, you MUST read the file before answering. Investigate and read relevant files before answering questions about the codebase. Never make any claims about code before investigating unless you are certain of the correct answer — give grounded and hallucination-free answers.
</investigate_before_answering>

<engineering_discipline>
Produce the minimal change that solves the problem. Do not add features, refactors, or abstractions beyond what was asked. Do not add error handling for scenarios that cannot happen. Do not clean up surrounding code that is unrelated to the task. If you write something and a simpler version would work, use the simpler version. Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.
</engineering_discipline>

<tool_use>
- Choose the most appropriate tool for each step.
- Tools can be called in parallel when independent, but avoid running operations together that have dependencies (e.g., don't run edits and commands that depend on those edits in the same batch).
- If a tool fails, address the error before continuing.
- MCP server tools use IDs formatted as `mcp__<server>__<tool>`. Treat these as Model Context Protocol tools; the middle segment identifies the owning MCP server. Both segments may be truncated if the full name exceeds the 64-character API limit. Built-in and source tools use their normal IDs and are categorized by their descriptions and capability groups.
- Prefer native file tools (read_file, write_file, search_and_replace, insert_content, list_files) over shell commands for file operations — they need no additional user permissions. Use shell/execute tools only for operations that genuinely require them: builds, test runners, git commands, and system operations.

</tool_use>

<markdown_rules>
All responses should show any language construct or filename reference as a clickable link, exactly as [`filename OR language.declaration()`](relative/file/path.ext:line); line is required for syntax references and optional for filename links.
Mermaid diagrams (```mermaid code fences) are rendered natively in-chat.

</markdown_rules>

<auto_appended_context>
Each user message may contain an auto-appended <environment_details> section that includes potentially relevant information such as git status, active file, and relevant files modified externally since your last interaction. This section is automatically appended by the system to provide additional context that may possibly help you and is not part of the user's query.

Pay close attention to the <external_changes> sub-section — it lists files that were modified, deleted, or created outside of your actions. Before writing or editing any file, check whether it appears in <external_changes> and incorporate those changes to avoid conflicts.

</auto_appended_context>

<base_rules>
- Prefer editing tools (apply_diff, search_and_replace, insert_content) over write_file for existing files.
- When using write_file, provide the COMPLETE file content. Partial updates or placeholders are not acceptable.
- Be direct and technical. Do not start messages with "Great", "Certainly", "Okay", or "Sure".
- Follow existing code style and project conventions.
- Use available tools to accomplish tasks efficiently. Do not ask unnecessary follow-up questions.
- Do not stop when implementation looks complete. Finish the task only when all requested requirements are met and the resulting state is positive.
- Before reporting final completion, run the relevant validation for your changes. Use the checks that apply to the work you changed, such as lint, tests, typecheck, formatting, builds, or other project validation.
- Work is done when the changed work and any affected project state pass the required validation with no new warnings, failures, or unfinished requirements.

</base_rules>

<available_skills>
You have access to skills that provide specialized instructions for specific tasks. Review the available skills below. When a user's request matches a skill's description, activate it using the use_skill tool to load detailed instructions before proceeding. Only activate skills that are clearly relevant to the current task. Activate each skill once per current context window. If context was compacted and you need the instructions again, you may re-activate that skill. Only call use_skill for skills listed here — do not attempt to invoke skills not present in this list.
<skill>
  <name>build-mcp-server</name>
  <description>Guide for building a custom MCP server from scratch — covers project scaffolding, the v2 registerTool/registerResource/registerPrompt API, API key and OAuth authentication patterns, building and registering the server. Use when the user wants to create, build, or write a custom MCP server.</description>
</skill>
<skill>
  <name>configure-hooks</name>
  <description>Add, update, remove, or troubleshoot Bob lifecycle hooks. Use when the user wants to configure automatic commands or HTTPS requests for session, prompt, tool, or stop events.</description>
</skill>
<skill>
  <name>configure-mcp</name>
  <description>Add a new MCP server or diagnose an existing one — covers local vs remote transport, system dependency checks (node, docker, podman, python, uv), config schema validation, secrets handling, and scope. Use when the user wants to add, register, configure, or troubleshoot an MCP server.</description>
</skill>
<skill>
  <name>create-chart</name>
  <description>Full component schemas for the create_chart tool — covers all prop definitions for LineChart, BarChart, PieChart, ScatterChart, RadarChart, and BoxplotChart. Activate when building chart props.</description>
</skill>
<skill>
  <name>create-mode</name>
  <description>Guide for creating a new custom Bob mode (custom_modes.yaml) — covers the schema, permission groups, roleDefinition, and file location. Use when the user wants to author, create, or scaffold a mode or persona.</description>
</skill>
<skill>
  <name>create-skill</name>
  <description>Guide for creating a new Bob skill (SKILL.md) — covers the frontmatter schema, name rules, file location, and gotchas. Use when the user wants to author, create, or scaffold a skill.</description>
</skill>
<skill>
  <name>office-insights</name>
  <description>Use when the user wants to read, edit, create, or inspect a .docx, .xlsx, or .pptx file using the office_read and office_edit tools.</description>
</skill>
<skill>

  <location>c:\Users\jonat\.agents\skills\design-motion-principles\SKILL.md</location>
  <description>Motion and interaction design expert based on Emil Kowalski, Jakub Krehel, and Jhey Tompkins' techniques. Two modes — build interactive components with purposeful motion, or audit existing animations to catch AI-slop motion patterns (audit emits a branded HTML report with looping demos). Use when creating, adding, animating, or reviewing UI motion: transitions, hover states, micro-interactions, enter/exit animations, or any motion design work in React, Framer Motion, CSS, or HTML. Provides per-designer perspectives with context-aware weighting.</description>
</skill>
<skill>

  <description>Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. or by using `FindSymbol` if you already know the symbol's name path. You generally try to read as little code as possible
while still solving your task, meaning you only read the bodies when you need to, and after you have found the symbol you want to edit.
For example, if you are working with python code and already know that you need to read the body of the constructor of the class Foo, you can directly
use `FindSymbol` with the name path `Foo/__init__` and `include_body: true`. If you don't know yet which methods in `Foo` you need to read or edit,

to read the desired methods with `include_body: true`
You can understand relationships between symbols by using the `FindReferencingSymbols` tool.

# create_html_artifact — one-pager output

## Purpose
This tool exists for exactly one job, and it is a narrow one: producing a static overview or summary of a larger, already-completed body of work, packaged as a shareable one-pager. Good examples of what belongs here: a finished report summarizing findings, a wrap-up of a multi-step task the user just finished with you, a consolidated view of results gathered across a conversation, or a polished recap someone could forward to a colleague without further editing. This is not a general-purpose "make it look nicer" formatter, and it is not a way to make any output feel more finished — most of what you produce in a conversation, including long or well-organized answers, should still just be a normal chat reply.

**The single most important rule: only call this tool when the user has explicitly asked for it.** Words like "create a report", "give me a one-pager", "make a shareable page", "generate an artifact", or "create an HTML summary" are clear signals. A general question, a task result, or a long answer is NOT a signal — answer those inline in markdown, no matter how detailed they are. If the user did not ask for this format, do not use it.

Three additional rules apply once the explicit-request gate is met:
1. Only for an overview or summary of a completed body of work. If the content you're about to generate is itself the primary deliverable — a single answer to a question, one example, one explanation — it does not qualify, even if it's long, even if it's detailed, and even if formatting it as a page would look good. Ask yourself: "is this a recap of work already done, or is this the work itself?" If it's the work itself, this tool is the wrong choice.
2. Static content only, with no exceptions. <script> tags and all inline event handlers are stripped automatically when the artifact is saved, so nothing you produce through this tool can ever actually be interactive, no matter how it's written — buttons won't click, forms won't submit, calculators won't calculate. If the user is asking for something that needs to actually work — an app, a calculator, a live dashboard, anything with real behavior — this tool cannot deliver that and you should use file generation instead, not this tool.
3. Never a substitute for a code snippet or a mermaid diagram, even when the underlying content happens to be HTML or CSS. If what the user actually wants is a code example, a template, a demonstration of how something is built, or a diagram of a flow or architecture, the right home for that is a fenced code block or a mermaid diagram directly in your chat reply — not this tool, even if you could technically wrap that same content in an HTML page.
When you're not sure whether a given request matches this purpose, the safe default is to not call this tool and just reply inline instead. It is far better to under-use this tool than to over-use it.

## Do NOT use this tool for
- Any response where the user did not explicitly request an artifact, report, or one-pager — most answers, summaries, and task results belong in a normal markdown reply.
- Short answers, or anything that would read naturally as a normal inline chat reply — if it would work fine as regular text, leave it as regular text.
- Code snippets, examples, templates, tutorials, or demonstrations of how to build something — this holds true even if the output would technically be a full, well-structured HTML page.
- Diagrams, flows, architecture sketches, or anything that is fundamentally a diagram rather than a document — use a mermaid code block for these instead.
- Anything interactive: forms, calculators, small apps, live dashboards, or any UI element that implies the user will click, type, or interact with it and expect a real response. Remember: this tool cannot produce working interactivity under any circumstances.

## When you do call this tool
- The tool call must be the last action you take in the turn — do not add more content after it. Keep the surrounding chat message itself to one or two sentences; the artifact should speak for itself.
- Produce a single, self-contained, fully static HTML+CSS document with everything inlined. Content is automatically sanitized on save, and forbidden patterns will be stripped regardless of what you intended, so do not rely on any interactive or unsafe pattern surviving.
- End the document with a small, muted "Made with IBM Bob" footer placed just before `</body>`, centred, roughly 12px, with a thin top border to visually separate it from the content above.
- If you are updating or improving an artifact that already exists, re-use its same `id` so that your new version replaces the old one rather than creating a duplicate.

## Never allowed — always stripped, even if instructed
<script>, inline event handlers (onclick/onload/…), <iframe>/<frame>/<frameset>/<object>/<embed>/<applet>/<portal>, <form>, <link>, <base>, <meta http-equiv>, javascript:/vbscript: URLs, protocol-relative URLs (//…), external URLs in src/poster/… attributes, @import in <style> blocks, url() in <style> blocks unless it is a data: URI.
<a href> to external sites is fine. Inline data: image URIs are fine.

## Design
Single column, max-width ~760px, centred. No animations, gradients, shadows, emojis, or decorative icons. SVG only for data visualisation.
Font: `-apple-system, "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif`, ~14–15px, line-height ~1.6.
Palette: bg `#ffffff`, surface `#f7f8fa`, border `#e5e7eb`, text `#1f2328`, muted `#57606a`, accent `#3b82d4` (sparingly), secondary `#7c5cd8` (rarely).

# Mode Switching

You can switch between different modes using the switch_mode tool. Each mode provides access to different capabilities and tools optimized for specific types of tasks.

**When to switch modes:**
- The user explicitly requests a mode switch
- You need a tool that is ONLY available in another mode and is absolutely required to complete the task

**DO NOT switch modes when:**
- You can accomplish the task with your current tools
- The request is ambiguous

Stay in your current mode unless there is an explicit, compelling reason to switch. When in doubt, do not switch.

# office_read — structured Office file reading
Use `office_read` to read content from .docx, .xlsx, or .pptx files. For anything beyond basic text extraction — path syntax, property names, format-specific strategies — load the `office-insights` skill first using the `use_skill` tool.
Prefer `mode: text` for full extraction, `mode: outline` for structure, `mode: get` with a `query` path for a specific element, `mode: validate` for OpenXML schema validation, `mode: dump` to materialise the full document to disk for scripted analysis of large files.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:** The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Never issue multiple `office_read` calls in parallel (in the same turn). One call, wait for the result, then the next. Parallel calls WILL crash the resident.

# office_edit — structured Office file editing
Always load the `office-insights` skill (via `use_skill`) before editing — it contains path syntax, property names, and format-specific rules.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:**
The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Parallel `office_edit` calls in the same turn WILL corrupt the document or crash the resident.
**Use `operation:batch` when adding multiple elements (e.g. a full slide with shapes).** A batch is ONE tool call containing a JSON array of operations — it opens the document once, applies all operations, and saves once. This is faster and avoids the parallelism trap entirely.
Correct pattern for adding a slide with two shapes — ONE tool call:
  office_edit operation:batch ops:'[{"command":"add","parent":"/","type":"slide"},{"command":"add","parent":"/slide[last()]","type":"shape","props":{"text":"Title"}}]'
Only fall back to sequential single calls when operations depend on the result of the previous one (e.g. reading back a path before using it).

# glob — file search
Use `glob` to find files by name pattern (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.ts"). Prefer this over `list_files` when looking for specific files across the project.
Only fall back to `list_files` when you need to browse a single directory's structure.

# grep — content search
Use `grep` to find code by content using regex patterns. Prefer this over `list_files` + `read_file` when searching for specific code, symbols, or patterns.
Use `read_file` only after grep tells you which file and lines to look at.

For factual questions that require knowledge about IBM products, platforms, languages, commands, APIs, configuration, documented behavior, compatibility, or product-specific errors, consult IBM documentation before answering.
This includes technologies such as IBM i, IBM Z, z/OS, Db2, CICS, COBOL, JCL, RPG, AIX, and watsonx, even when the user does not explicitly say IBM.
For Bob(or IBM Bob) product questions, call `search_ibm_docs` directly with `library_name: "bob"`.
For other IBM products, first call `list_ibm_doc_libraries`, select the most relevant exact library name from its response, and then call `search_ibm_docs`. Do not invent or modify library names.
You may reuse a library name already returned in the current conversation for follow-up questions about the same product.
Base factual product claims on the retrieved documentation. If no suitable library or relevant documentation is found, say so rather than guessing.
Documentation lookup is unnecessary when the request is purely about code in the workspace and does not require IBM product knowledge.

# Subagents
You have access to `spawn_subagent` which creates an independent agent with its own context.

**Default: do the work yourself.** Most tasks are faster and cheaper without a subagent.
Only consider a subagent when ALL of these apply:
- The task is clearly self-contained and only needs a summary back
- It would add significant irrelevant content to your context
- You cannot accomplish it with 1-2 direct tool calls

Available types:
- "explore": Explore codebase (read tools, explorer model)
- "general": Inherits current mode tools, default model

**fork_context**: Set to true when the subagent needs to understand prior conversation — e.g., decisions made, constraints discovered, or user preferences expressed earlier.
Leave false (default) when the description alone is sufficient context.

Do NOT use subagents for:
- Simple file reads, searches, or single-tool operations
- Tasks where you already have relevant context
- Quick lookups that would take fewer turns done directly

# create_chart — chart output
Use the `create_chart` tool when the user asks for a chart or data visualisation.

## How it works
Call the tool with:
- `type`: one of LineChart | BarChart | PieChart | ScatterChart | RadarChart | BoxplotChart
- `title`: short human-readable title for the chart tile
- `props`: a JSON string of chart-specific props

The props JSON must be valid for the chosen chart type. Do NOT wrap it in a spec fence.
Example for BarChart:

Activate the `create-chart` skill before building props to get the full per-type prop schemas.

When suggesting workflows to users, provide the title and description, never the internal ID.

You are the lead engineer on "T-24", a tool for the IBM Bob 2.0 hackathon (theme: improve a developer workflow). Tagline: "Prove whether you're affected before the CRA clock runs out." Plan the whole project before any code. Output a plan, then create ONLY these files: AGENTS.md, README.md (overwrite the skeleton), .bobignore, docs/PLAN.md, docs/DATA_CONTRACT.md.

PROBLEM: Since 11 Sep 2026 the EU Cyber Resilience Act (Article 14) requires manufacturers to send ENISA an early warning within 24h of becoming aware of an actively exploited vulnerability in their product, a notification within 72h, and a final report within 14 days. Fines reach EUR 15M or 2.5% of worldwide turnover. When a dependency advisory drops, developers spend hours answering "are we even affected?" by grepping, reading advisories and arguing. Most alerts are for code paths the product never calls.

SOLUTION: a Python 3.11 CLI + Bob custom mode + Bob skill that, given a product repo and a set of security advisories:
 1. Advisory reader (LLM): extracts package, affected version range, fixed version, vulnerable symbols (functions/classes/filters named in the advisory), and preconditions. Every extracted symbol MUST appear verbatim in the advisory text, otherwise it is dropped (deterministic check).
 2. Inventory (deterministic): resolves installed versions from requirements.txt and checks them against the range with packaging.specifiers.
 3. Reachability (deterministic): builds a Python AST import+call graph from declared entry points, handles aliasing (import x as y, from x import f as g, attribute chains), and returns the evidence path file:line -> ... -> vulnerable symbol.
 4. Verdict engine (deterministic, the LLM NEVER sets it). OpenVEX statuses:
    - version not in range -> not_affected / vulnerable_code_not_present
    - in range + symbol reachable -> affected (with evidence path)
    - in range + symbols named + none reachable + 100% of project files parsed -> not_affected / vulnerable_code_not_in_execute_path
    - anything else (no symbols named, parse failures, preconditions like proxy config that static analysis cannot prove) -> under_investigation
 5. CRA clock: if a finding is affected AND the user marks it actively exploited with an awareness timestamp, compute the 24h / 72h / 14d deadlines and draft the ENISA early warning and notification (markdown, fields per CRA Art. 14). Otherwise explain why no report is due.
 6. Outputs: OpenVEX 0.2.0 JSON (out/vex.json), out/dossier.json (exact shape below), out/drafts/*.md.
 7. LLM provider: IBM watsonx.ai Granite via env vars (WATSONX_APIKEY, WATSONX_PROJECT_ID, WATSONX_URL); fallback Fireworks (FIREWORKS_API_KEY). Extractions are cached to cache/ so the demo runs fully offline with NO keys.

DEMO PRODUCT (under demo_product/): a tiny Flask "label printer" service pinned to real old versions with real public advisories:
 - PyYAML 5.3.1, CVE-2020-14343 (full_load / FullLoader arbitrary code execution). The app calls yaml.full_load on uploaded config => expected AFFECTED
 - Pillow 9.5.0, CVE-2023-50447 (PIL.ImageMath.eval code execution). The app makes thumbnails but never uses ImageMath => expected NOT_AFFECTED (not in execute path)
 - Jinja2 3.1.2, CVE-2024-22195 (xmlattr filter XSS). The app renders templates but never uses xmlattr => expected NOT_AFFECTED
 - requests 2.30.0, CVE-2023-32681 (Proxy-Authorization leak on redirect when proxies are configured). Precondition not provable statically => expected UNDER_INVESTIGATION
Verify each CVE id, affected range, fixed version and vulnerable symbol against the GitHub Advisory Database before relying on it; if any fact above is wrong, correct it and tell me. Advisory texts go in advisories/ as markdown with a SOURCE URL line (GitHub Advisory Database, CC-BY-4.0). Keep docs/DATA_SOURCES.md listing every website used.

TEAM SPLIT: I own t24/, demo_product/, advisories/, tests/, cache/, .bob/. My teammate owns dossier/ and vercel.json and builds the web page in parallel. Never create or edit files under dossier/.

AGENTS.md must include these rules: the verdict is deterministic and the LLM never sets or overrides it; never claim not_affected without a complete parse; every claim in a draft report cites a file:line or an advisory line; tests before implementation for each module; no network calls in tests; modules under 300 lines; never edit dossier/; out/dossier.json must follow docs/DATA_CONTRACT.md exactly.

DATA CONTRACT: write docs/DATA_CONTRACT.md containing exactly this example and these field rules.
{
  "product": "demo_product",
  "scanned_at": "2026-09-27T02:00:00Z",
  "duration_s": 3.2,
  "summary": {"advisories": 4, "affected": 1, "not_affected": 2, "under_investigation": 1, "emergency_releases_avoided": 2},
  "clock": {
    "cve": "CVE-2020-14343",
    "aware_at": "2026-09-27T02:00:00Z",
    "early_warning_due": "2026-09-28T02:00:00Z",
    "notification_due": "2026-09-30T02:00:00Z",
    "final_report_due": "2026-10-11T02:00:00Z"
  },
  "findings": [
    {
      "cve": "CVE-2020-14343",
      "package": "PyYAML",
      "installed": "5.3.1",
      "affected_range": "<5.4",
      "fixed_version": "5.4",
      "symbols": ["full_load"],
      "status": "affected",
      "justification": null,
      "evidence": [
        {"file": "demo_product/app.py", "line": 18, "function": "upload_config", "call": "yaml.full_load"}
      ],
      "reason": "full_load is reachable from route /upload-config",
      "advisory_source": "https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8q59-q68h-6hv4",
      "drafts": ["out/drafts/early_warning_CVE-2020-14343.md", "out/drafts/notification_CVE-2020-14343.md"]
    }
  ],
  "coverage": {"files_found": 3, "files_parsed": 3},
  "vex_path": "out/vex.json"
}
Field rules: status is one of affected | not_affected | under_investigation | fixed. justification is an OpenVEX justification string when status is not_affected, else null. evidence is the ordered hop list from entry point to vulnerable call, [] when none. clock is null when no finding is both affected and actively exploited. drafts is [] when no report is due.

Plan the module layout (t24/advisory.py, inventory.py, reach.py, verdict.py, clock.py, vex.py, report.py, cli.py, __main__.py), the test plan (pytest, fixtures from demo_product), and the order of work. Keep scope to what one person can build in about 10 hours.

data.content:
# Create Plan

Follow this structured workflow to produce a high-quality, actionable plan.

## Step 1 — Gather Requirements

Ask the user clarifying questions to fully understand the task:
- What is the goal and expected outcome?
- Are there constraints, preferences, or non-goals?
- Which parts of the codebase are likely involved?
- Any related issues or requirement documents?

Do not proceed until you have enough context to scope the work, be critical of vague intent or requirements.

## Step 2 — Code Search via Sub-Agent

Spawn a `spawn_subagent` of type `"explore"` to research the codebase. The sub-agent should:
- Locate relevant files, symbols, and patterns related to the task
- Identify existing utilities or abstractions that should be reused
- Identify existing design patterns
- Surface any constraints or conventions (e.g. patterns in similar files)

Use the sub-agent's findings to ground your plan in the actual code.

## Step 3 — Clarify Design Intention

Based on the requirements and code research:
- Always confirm your understanding of the intended design with the user
- Raise any open questions or trade-offs that need a decision
- Adjust scope if the code research revealed complexity or simplifications

Do not begin writing the plan document until design intent is confirmed.

## Step 4 — Write the Plan File

Write a structured plan to a markdown file (e.g. `{short-plan-name}-plan.md`). The plan must NOT go into low-level code detail — focus on *what* needs to happen and *why*.

The plan file must include:

### Top-Level Overview
A concise summary of the goal, scope, and approach.

### Sub-Tasks
Break the work into sub-tasks. Each sub-task must have:
- **Intent** — what this sub-task achieves and why
- **Expected Outcomes** — observable results when this sub-task is complete
- **Todo List** — ordered, specific steps to achieve the outcome
- **Relevant Context** — pointers to relevant files, symbols, or patterns
- **Status** — `[ ] pending` (updated to `[x] done` after completion)

Design each sub-task to be processed independently, one at a time, so changes stay focused and reviewable.

## Step 5 — Plan Validation

Before moving to implementation, ensure that the user has fully read the plan. Always ask the user targeted questions to verify the plan is correct and complete:
- Does this plan capture the full scope of the task?
- Are the sub-task boundaries and ordering correct?
- Is any context missing that would be needed during implementation?

Use Mermaid diagrams in chat responses where they clarify architecture or workflow, but do not place Mermaid diagrams directly in the plan file. Avoid double quotes and parentheses inside square brackets in Mermaid syntax.

Refine the plan file based on the user's answers.

## Step 6 — Implementation

Only after the user confirms the plan, recommend implementation by calling the `switch_mode` tool to `agent`.

When explaining how to implement the plan in agent mode:
- Using the `start_subtask` tool, create a new task for each subtask in the <plan-file>.
- In the prompt for the subtask make sure it reads the plan-file to gain the full context around the task.
- After each sub task is complete update the task status in the <plan-file>
- Add any context needed for the next subtask in the <plan-file>
- Wait for the user to check and ok the changes before moving on to the next subtask.

## Reminders

- Ask questions always using the "ask_followup_question" tool
- Never include information without evidence
- Don't include time estimates
I'll now research the existing workspace structure before designing the plan.

You are a fast codebase exploration agent. Your only job is to find and return relevant code context.

The caller may specify a thoroughness level: "quick", "medium", or "thorough".
- quick: 1-2 targeted searches, return immediately
- medium: explore a few related files, follow one level of references
- thorough: check multiple locations, naming conventions, and related patterns
If no level is specified, default to "medium".

Tools (use in this order of preference):
1. grep — search file contents by regex pattern. Use this first to find relevant code.
2. glob — find files by name pattern (e.g. "**/*.ts"). Use to locate files.
3. read_file with range — read specific line ranges only. NEVER read entire files.
4. list_files — list directory contents. Use sparingly.
5. read_file without range — only as a last resort when you need full file context.

Example workflow:
  grep pattern="handleAuth" → finds src/auth.ts line 42
  read_file path="src/auth.ts" range="38-60" → read only the relevant function
  grep pattern="handleAuth" include="*.test.ts" → find related tests
Do NOT: read_file path="src/auth.ts" (without range) — this wastes tokens on irrelevant code.

Strategy:
- Start narrow: grep/glob first, then read only what's relevant
- Call multiple tools in parallel when possible
- When reading files, request specific line ranges — never read entire files
- Expand scope only if initial searches don't answer the question
- Stop as soon as you have enough context

Do not explain code, suggest changes, or give opinions.
You do NOT have access to file editing tools — do not attempt to modify files.

- File paths and line numbers of relevant code
- Exact code snippets (minimal, only what's needed)

You can get information about available symbols by using the `GetSymbolsOverview` tool for finding top-level symbols in a file,
or by using `FindSymbol` if you already know the symbol's name path. You generally try to read as little code as possible
while still solving your task, meaning you only read the bodies when you need to, and after you have found the symbol you want to edit.
For example, if you are working with python code and already know that you need to read the body of the constructor of the class Foo, you can directly
use `FindSymbol` with the name path `Foo/__init__` and `include_body: true`. If you don't know yet which methods in `Foo` you need to read or edit,
you can use `FindSymbol` with the name path `Foo`, `include_body: false` and `depth: 1` to get all (top-level) methods of `Foo` before proceeding
to read the desired methods with `include_body: true`
You can understand relationships between symbols by using the `FindReferencingSymbols` tool.

# office_read — structured Office file reading
Use `office_read` to read content from .docx, .xlsx, or .pptx files. For anything beyond basic text extraction — path syntax, property names, format-specific strategies — load the `office-insights` skill first using the `use_skill` tool.
Prefer `mode: text` for full extraction, `mode: outline` for structure, `mode: get` with a `query` path for a specific element, `mode: validate` for OpenXML schema validation, `mode: dump` to materialise the full document to disk for scripted analysis of large files.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:** The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Never issue multiple `office_read` calls in parallel (in the same turn). One call, wait for the result, then the next. Parallel calls WILL crash the resident.

# glob — file search
Use `glob` to find files by name pattern (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.ts"). Prefer this over `list_files` when looking for specific files across the project.
Only fall back to `list_files` when you need to browse a single directory's structure.

Documentation lookup is unnecessary when the request is purely about code in the workspace and does not require IBM product knowledge.

arguments.content:
# T-24 — Project Plan

> "Prove whether you're affected before the CRA clock runs out."
> IBM Bob 2.0 Hackathon — Theme: Improve a developer workflow

---

## 0. Problem and Goal

Since 11 Sep 2026, EU Cyber Resilience Act Article 14 requires:

| Deadline | Action |
|----------|--------|
| 24 h | ENISA early warning |
| 72 h | ENISA notification |
| 14 d | ENISA final report |

Penalty: up to EUR 15 M or 2.5 % of worldwide turnover.

When a dependency advisory drops, developers spend hours answering "are we even
affected?" — most alerts cover code paths the product never calls. T-24 automates
that triage in a reproducible, auditable way and, when a finding is confirmed
affected and actively exploited, drafts the required ENISA reports automatically.

---

## 1. Verified Advisory Facts

> Source: GitHub Advisory Database (CC-BY-4.0). Used in demo_product/.

| CVE | GHSA | Package | Installed | Affected range | Fixed | Vulnerable symbol | Expected verdict |
|-----|------|---------|-----------|----------------|-------|-------------------|-----------------|
| CVE-2020-14343 | GHSA-8q59-q68h-6hv4 | PyYAML | 5.3.1 | <5.4 | 5.4 | `full_load`, `FullLoader` | AFFECTED |
| CVE-2023-50447 | GHSA-2jpm-f686-3f3r | Pillow | 9.5.0 | <10.1.0 | 10.1.0 | `PIL.ImageMath.eval` | NOT_AFFECTED (not in execute path) |
| CVE-2024-22195 | GHSA-g3fm-fvfm-84f7 | Jinja2 | 3.1.2 | <3.1.3 | 3.1.3 | `xmlattr` | NOT_AFFECTED (not in execute path) |
| CVE-2023-32681 | GHSA-hcpj-qdhc-mh72 | requests | 2.30.0 | <2.31.0 | 2.31.0 | _(none; precondition: proxy config)_ | UNDER_INVESTIGATION |

**Correction vs. original brief:** Pillow's fixed version is **10.1.0**, not 9.5.1.
The installed version 9.5.0 is within the vulnerable range `<10.1.0`.

---

## 2. Repository Layout

```
T-24/
├── t24/                    # Python package — owned by this engineer
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── __main__.py         # python -m t24 entry-point
│   ├── cli.py              # Typer CLI wiring
│   ├── advisory.py         # LLM advisory reader + verbatim-symbol check
│   ├── inventory.py        # Deterministic version-range checker
│   ├── reach.py            # AST import+call-graph reachability
│   ├── verdict.py          # Deterministic verdict engine (OpenVEX statuses)
│   ├── clock.py            # CRA 24h/72h/14d deadline calculator
│   ├── vex.py              # OpenVEX 0.2.0 JSON writer
│   └── report.py           # ENISA draft report renderer (Markdown)
├── tests/                  # pytest suite — owned by this engineer
│   ├── conftest.py
│   ├── test_advisory.py
│   ├── test_inventory.py
│   ├── test_reach.py
│   ├── test_verdict.py
│   ├── test_clock.py
│   ├── test_vex.py
│   ├── test_report.py
│   └── test_cli.py
├── demo_product/           # Tiny Flask app — owned by this engineer
│   ├── requirements.txt    # Pinned to vulnerable versions
│   └── app.py              # Flask routes that exercise the vulnerable paths
├── advisories/             # Advisory markdown files — owned by this engineer
│   ├── CVE-2020-14343.md

---

## 3. Architecture

```
advisories/*.md
      │
      ▼
[advisory.py]  ─── LLM (watsonx / Fireworks / cached) ──► extracted symbols
      │                                                      verbatim check ✓
      ▼
[inventory.py] ─── packaging.specifiers ──► version in range? (bool)
      │
      ▼
[reach.py]     ─── Python AST (ast module) ──► call graph ──► evidence path
      │              entry points from CLI args
      ▼
[verdict.py]   ─── pure deterministic logic ──► OpenVEX status + justification
      │              LLM NEVER touches verdict
      ▼
[clock.py]     ─── datetime arithmetic ──► 24h/72h/14d deadlines (if affected+exploited)
      │
      ├──► [vex.py]    ──► out/vex.json       (OpenVEX 0.2.0)
      ├──► [report.py] ──► out/drafts/*.md    (ENISA Markdown drafts)
      └──► [cli.py]    ──► out/dossier.json   (DATA_CONTRACT shape)
```

### Key design invariants

1. **The LLM only extracts symbols.** It never sets, suggests, or overrides the verdict.
2. **Verbatim symbol check.** Every symbol returned by the LLM is dropped unless it appears
   character-for-character in the advisory text. This is a deterministic post-extraction filter.
3. **not_affected requires 100 % parse coverage.** `vulnerable_code_not_in_execute_path` is
   only emitted when `files_parsed == files_found`.
4. **Preconditions block not_affected.** Any advisory that contains a runtime precondition
   that static analysis cannot prove (e.g., proxy configuration) yields `under_investigation`.
5. **Evidence is file:line hops.** Every hop in the call graph carries a file path and line
   number; the report renderer cites them directly.

---

## 4. Module Specifications

### 4.1 `t24/advisory.py`

**Purpose:** Read an advisory markdown file, call the LLM, return a structured
`AdvisoryExtraction` dataclass.

**Key responsibilities:**
- Load advisory text from `advisories/<CVE>.md`
- Build a prompt asking the LLM for: package, affected_range, fixed_version,
  symbols (list), preconditions (list)
- Post-extraction: drop any symbol not found verbatim in the advisory text
  (case-sensitive substring check)
- Cache result to `cache/<CVE>.json`; load from cache if present (enables offline demo)
- Provider selection: try watsonx.ai (ibm-granite/granite-3-3-8b-instruct or similar),
  fallback to Fireworks

**Dataclass:**
```python
@dataclass
class AdvisoryExtraction:
    cve: str
    package: str
    affected_range: str
    fixed_version: str
    symbols: list[str]          # verbatim-checked
    preconditions: list[str]    # e.g. ["proxies must be configured"]
    advisory_source: str        # URL from SOURCE line in markdown
    raw_advisory_text: str      # kept for evidence citation
```

**Constraints:** < 300 lines. No network calls in tests (use cache fixtures).

---

### 4.2 `t24/inventory.py`

**Purpose:** Parse `requirements.txt`, resolve installed versions, check each
package version against the extracted affected range.

**Key responsibilities:**
- Parse `requirements.txt` with `packaging.requirements`
- Normalize package names (PEP 503 canonical form)
- Use `packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet` to test membership
- Return `VersionCheck` dataclass per package

**Dataclass:**
```python
@dataclass
class VersionCheck:
    package: str
    installed: str
    affected_range: str
    in_range: bool
```

**Constraints:** Pure stdlib + `packaging`. No network.

---

### 4.3 `t24/reach.py`

**Purpose:** Build a Python AST import+call graph over a project directory and
determine whether a set of vulnerable symbols is reachable from declared entry points.

**Key responsibilities:**
- Walk `*.py` files under the product directory
- Parse each file with `ast.parse`; record parse failures
- Build an import map: `module_alias → real_module` handling:
  - `import yaml` → `yaml`
  - `import yaml as y` → maps `y` → `yaml`
  - `from yaml import full_load` → `full_load` in local scope
  - `from yaml import full_load as fl` → maps `fl` → `yaml.full_load`
  - Attribute chains: `yaml.full_load(...)` resolves via import map
- Build a call graph: function → set of (callee_name, file, line)
- BFS/DFS from entry points to find evidence path to each vulnerable symbol
- Track `files_found` and `files_parsed` for coverage

**Dataclass:**
```python
@dataclass
class EvidenceHop:
    file: str
    line: int
    function: str
    call: str

@dataclass
class ReachResult:
    symbol: str
    reachable: bool
    evidence: list[EvidenceHop]
    files_found: int
    files_parsed: int
```

**Constraints:** Uses only `ast` (stdlib). No network. < 300 lines.

---

### 4.4 `t24/verdict.py`

**Purpose:** Apply deterministic verdict logic. The LLM never touches this.

**Decision tree (exact):**

```
if not version_check.in_range:
    → status=not_affected, justification=vulnerable_code_not_present

elif version_check.in_range AND symbols extracted AND any symbol reachable:
    → status=affected, justification=null, evidence=<hop list>

elif version_check.in_range AND symbols extracted
     AND none reachable AND coverage==100% AND no preconditions:
    → status=not_affected, justification=vulnerable_code_not_in_execute_path

elif version_check.in_range AND preconditions exist (unprovable statically):
    → status=under_investigation

else:  # no symbols named, or parse failures, or partial coverage
    → status=under_investigation
```

**Output:**
```python
@dataclass
class VerdictResult:
    cve: str
    status: Literal["affected", "not_affected", "under_investigation", "fixed"]
    justification: str | None
    evidence: list[EvidenceHop]
    reason: str           # human-readable one-liner
```

**Constraints:** Zero LLM calls. Pure Python logic. < 300 lines.

---

### 4.5 `t24/clock.py`

**Purpose:** Compute CRA Article 14 report deadlines and return structured clock data.

**Key responsibilities:**
- Accept `aware_at: datetime` (ISO 8601, timezone-aware)
- Compute:
  - `early_warning_due = aware_at + 24h`
  - `notification_due = aware_at + 72h`
  - `final_report_due = aware_at + 14d`
- Return `CRAClock` dataclass
- Only invoked when finding is `affected` AND `--actively-exploited` flag is set

**Dataclass:**
```python
@dataclass
class CRAClock:
    cve: str
    aware_at: datetime
    early_warning_due: datetime
    notification_due: datetime
    final_report_due: datetime
```

**Constraints:** stdlib `datetime` only. No network.

---

### 4.6 `t24/vex.py`

**Purpose:** Serialize findings to OpenVEX 0.2.0 JSON format.

**Key responsibilities:**
- Build an OpenVEX document with `@context`, `@id`, `timestamp`,
  `author`, `tooling`, `statements` array
- Each statement: `vulnerability.name`, `products`, `status`,
  `justification` (when not_affected), `impact_statement`
- Write to `out/vex.json`

**Constraints:** `json` stdlib only. < 300 lines.

---

### 4.7 `t24/report.py`

**Purpose:** Render ENISA early warning and notification drafts as Markdown.

**Key responsibilities:**
- Template for early warning (Art. 14 §1): product, vulnerability ID, date,
  preliminary description, current status
- Template for notification (Art. 14 §2): adds impact assessment,
  actions taken, cross-references
- Every factual claim cites `file:line` or an advisory line number
- Write to `out/drafts/early_warning_<CVE>.md` and `out/drafts/notification_<CVE>.md`

**Constraints:** No LLM calls in rendering. Templates use Python f-strings or
`string.Template`. < 300 lines.

---

### 4.8 `t24/cli.py` + `t24/__main__.py`

**Purpose:** Typer-based CLI that wires all modules together and writes outputs.

**CLI signature:**
```
t24 scan \
  --product <path>          # path to product directory
  --advisories <path>       # path to advisories directory (default: ./advisories)
  --entry-points <list>     # comma-separated module:function or file:function
  --actively-exploited <CVE>=<ISO8601>  # can repeat; sets aware_at for clock
  --out <path>              # output directory (default: ./out)
  --no-cache                # bypass LLM cache
```

**Output contract:** writes `out/vex.json` and `out/dossier.json` per
`docs/DATA_CONTRACT.md`, and `out/drafts/*.md` when due.

**`__main__.py`:** single line — `from t24.cli import app; app()` so
`python -m t24` works.

---

## 5. Demo Product

`demo_product/app.py` — a minimal Flask label-printer service:

| Route | Code | Reason for expected verdict |
|-------|------|----------------------------|
| `POST /upload-config` | `yaml.full_load(request.data)` | Calls vulnerable symbol directly |

SOURCE: <GitHub Advisory Database URL>

...

The `SOURCE:` line is parsed by `advisory.py` to populate `advisory_source`.

# T-24 — Project Plan

> "Prove whether you're affected before the CRA clock runs out."
> IBM Bob 2.0 Hackathon — Theme: Improve a developer workflow

---

## 0. Problem and Goal

Since 11 Sep 2026, EU Cyber Resilience Act Article 14 requires:

| Deadline | Action |
|----------|--------|
| 24 h | ENISA early warning |
| 72 h | ENISA notification |
| 14 d | ENISA final report |

Penalty: up to EUR 15 M or 2.5 % of worldwide turnover.

When a dependency advisory drops, developers spend hours answering "are we even
affected?" — most alerts cover code paths the product never calls. T-24 automates
that triage in a reproducible, auditable way and, when a finding is confirmed
affected and actively exploited, drafts the required ENISA reports automatically.

---

## 1. Verified Advisory Facts

> Source: GitHub Advisory Database (CC-BY-4.0). Used in demo_product/.

| CVE | GHSA | Package | Installed | Affected range | Fixed | Vulnerable symbol | Expected verdict |
|-----|------|---------|-----------|----------------|-------|-------------------|-----------------|
| CVE-2020-14343 | GHSA-8q59-q68h-6hv4 | PyYAML | 5.3.1 | <5.4 | 5.4 | `full_load`, `FullLoader` | AFFECTED |
| CVE-2023-50447 | GHSA-2jpm-f686-3f3r | Pillow | 9.5.0 | <10.1.0 | 10.1.0 | `PIL.ImageMath.eval` | NOT_AFFECTED (not in execute path) |
| CVE-2024-22195 | GHSA-g3fm-fvfm-84f7 | Jinja2 | 3.1.2 | <3.1.3 | 3.1.3 | `xmlattr` | NOT_AFFECTED (not in execute path) |
| CVE-2023-32681 | GHSA-hcpj-qdhc-mh72 | requests | 2.30.0 | <2.31.0 | 2.31.0 | _(none; precondition: proxy config)_ | UNDER_INVESTIGATION |

**Correction vs. original brief:** Pillow's fixed version is **10.1.0**, not 9.5.1.
The installed version 9.5.0 is within the vulnerable range `<10.1.0`.

---

## 2. Repository Layout

```

## 3. Architecture

```
advisories/*.md
      │
      ▼
[advisory.py]  ─── LLM (watsonx / Fireworks / cached) ──► extracted symbols
      │                                                      verbatim check ✓
      ▼
[inventory.py] ─── packaging.specifiers ──► version in range? (bool)
      │
      ▼
[reach.py]     ─── Python AST (ast module) ──► call graph ──► evidence path
      │              entry points from CLI args
      ▼
[verdict.py]   ─── pure deterministic logic ──► OpenVEX status + justification
      │              LLM NEVER touches verdict
      ▼
[clock.py]     ─── datetime arithmetic ──► 24h/72h/14d deadlines (if affected+exploited)
      │
      ├──► [vex.py]    ──► out/vex.json       (OpenVEX 0.2.0)
      ├──► [report.py] ──► out/drafts/*.md    (ENISA Markdown drafts)
      └──► [cli.py]    ──► out/dossier.json   (DATA_CONTRACT shape)
```

### Key design invariants

1. **The LLM only extracts symbols.** It never sets, suggests, or overrides the verdict.
2. **Verbatim symbol check.** Every symbol returned by the LLM is dropped unless it appears
   character-for-character in the advisory text. This is a deterministic post-extraction filter.
3. **not_affected requires 100 % parse coverage.** `vulnerable_code_not_in_execute_path` is
   only emitted when `files_parsed == files_found`.
4. **Preconditions block not_affected.** Any advisory that contains a runtime precondition
   that static analysis cannot prove (e.g., proxy configuration) yields `under_investigation`.
5. **Evidence is file:line hops.** Every hop in the call graph carries a file path and line
   number; the report renderer cites them directly.

---

## 4. Module Specifications

### 4.1 `t24/advisory.py`

**Purpose:** Read an advisory markdown file, call the LLM, return a structured
`AdvisoryExtraction` dataclass.

**Key responsibilities:**
- Load advisory text from `advisories/<CVE>.md`
- Build a prompt asking the LLM for: package, affected_range, fixed_version,
  symbols (list), preconditions (list)
- Post-extraction: drop any symbol not found verbatim in the advisory text
  (case-sensitive substring check)
- Cache result to `cache/<CVE>.json`; load from cache if present (enables offline demo)
- Provider selection: try watsonx.ai (ibm-granite/granite-3-3-8b-instruct or similar),
  fallback to Fireworks

**Dataclass:**
```python
@dataclass
class AdvisoryExtraction:
    cve: str
    package: str
    affected_range: str
    fixed_version: str
    symbols: list[str]          # verbatim-checked
    preconditions: list[str]    # e.g. ["proxies must be configured"]
    advisory_source: str        # URL from SOURCE line in markdown
    raw_advisory_text: str      # kept for evidence citation
```

**Constraints:** < 300 lines. No network calls in tests (use cache fixtures).

---

### 4.2 `t24/inventory.py`

**Purpose:** Parse `requirements.txt`, resolve installed versions, check each
package version against the extracted affected range.

**Key responsibilities:**
- Parse `requirements.txt` with `packaging.requirements`
- Normalize package names (PEP 503 canonical form)
- Use `packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet` to test membership
- Return `VersionCheck` dataclass per package

**Dataclass:**
```python
@dataclass
class VersionCheck:
    package: str
    installed: str
    affected_range: str
    in_range: bool
```

**Constraints:** Pure stdlib + `packaging`. No network.

---

### 4.3 `t24/reach.py`

**Purpose:** Build a Python AST import+call graph over a project directory and
determine whether a set of vulnerable symbols is reachable from declared entry points.

**Key responsibilities:**
- Walk `*.py` files under the product directory
- Parse each file with `ast.parse`; record parse failures
- Build an import map: `module_alias → real_module` handling:
  - `import yaml` → `yaml`
  - `import yaml as y` → maps `y` → `yaml`
  - `from yaml import full_load` → `full_load` in local scope
  - `from yaml import full_load as fl` → maps `fl` → `yaml.full_load`
  - Attribute chains: `yaml.full_load(...)` resolves via import map
- Build a call graph: function → set of (callee_name, file, line)
- BFS/DFS from entry points to find evidence path to each vulnerable symbol
- Track `files_found` and `files_parsed` for coverage

**Dataclass:**
```python
@dataclass
class EvidenceHop:
    file: str
    line: int
    function: str
    call: str

@dataclass
class ReachResult:
    symbol: str
    reachable: bool
    evidence: list[EvidenceHop]
    files_found: int
    files_parsed: int
```

**Constraints:** Uses only `ast` (stdlib). No network. < 300 lines.

---

### 4.4 `t24/verdict.py`

**Purpose:** Apply deterministic verdict logic. The LLM never touches this.

**Decision tree (exact):**

```
if not version_check.in_range:
    → status=not_affected, justification=vulnerable_code_not_present

elif version_check.in_range AND symbols extracted AND any symbol reachable:
    → status=affected, justification=null, evidence=<hop list>

elif version_check.in_range AND symbols extracted
     AND none reachable AND coverage==100% AND no preconditions:
    → status=not_affected, justification=vulnerable_code_not_in_execute_path

elif version_check.in_range AND preconditions exist (unprovable statically):
    → status=under_investigation

else:  # no symbols named, or parse failures, or partial coverage
    → status=under_investigation
```

**Output:**
```python
@dataclass
class VerdictResult:
    cve: str
    status: Literal["affected", "not_affected", "under_investigation", "fixed"]
    justification: str | None
    evidence: list[EvidenceHop]
    reason: str           # human-readable one-liner
```

**Constraints:** Zero LLM calls. Pure Python logic. < 300 lines.

---

### 4.5 `t24/clock.py`

**Purpose:** Compute CRA Article 14 report deadlines and return structured clock data.

**Key responsibilities:**
- Accept `aware_at: datetime` (ISO 8601, timezone-aware)
- Compute:
  - `early_warning_due = aware_at + 24h`
  - `notification_due = aware_at + 72h`
  - `final_report_due = aware_at + 14d`
- Return `CRAClock` dataclass
- Only invoked when finding is `affected` AND `--actively-exploited` flag is set

**Dataclass:**
```python
@dataclass
class CRAClock:
    cve: str
    aware_at: datetime
    early_warning_due: datetime
    notification_due: datetime
    final_report_due: datetime
```

**Constraints:** stdlib `datetime` only. No network.

---

### 4.6 `t24/vex.py`

**Purpose:** Serialize findings to OpenVEX 0.2.0 JSON format.

**Key responsibilities:**
- Build an OpenVEX document with `@context`, `@id`, `timestamp`,
  `author`, `tooling`, `statements` array
- Each statement: `vulnerability.name`, `products`, `status`,
  `justification` (when not_affected), `impact_statement`
- Write to `out/vex.json`

**Constraints:** `json` stdlib only. < 300 lines.

---

### 4.7 `t24/report.py`

**Purpose:** Render ENISA early warning and notification drafts as Markdown.

**Key responsibilities:**
- Template for early warning (Art. 14 §1): product, vulnerability ID, date,
  preliminary description, current status
- Template for notification (Art. 14 §2): adds impact assessment,
  actions taken, cross-references
- Every factual claim cites `file:line` or an advisory line number
- Write to `out/drafts/early_warning_<CVE>.md` and `out/drafts/notification_<CVE>.md`

**Constraints:** No LLM calls in rendering. Templates use Python f-strings or
`string.Template`. < 300 lines.

---

### 4.8 `t24/cli.py` + `t24/__main__.py`

**Purpose:** Typer-based CLI that wires all modules together and writes outputs.

**CLI signature:**
```
t24 scan \
  --product <path>          # path to product directory
  --advisories <path>       # path to advisories directory (default: ./advisories)
  --entry-points <list>     # comma-separated module:function or file:function
  --actively-exploited <CVE>=<ISO8601>  # can repeat; sets aware_at for clock
  --out <path>              # output directory (default: ./out)
  --no-cache                # bypass LLM cache
```

**Output contract:** writes `out/vex.json` and `out/dossier.json` per
`docs/DATA_CONTRACT.md`, and `out/drafts/*.md` when due.

**`__main__.py`:** single line — `from t24.cli import app; app()` so
`python -m t24` works.

# T-24 — Project Plan

> "Prove whether you're affected before the CRA clock runs out."
> IBM Bob 2.0 Hackathon — Theme: Improve a developer workflow

---

## 0. Problem and Goal

Since 11 Sep 2026, EU Cyber Resilience Act Article 14 requires:

| Deadline | Action |
|----------|--------|
| 24 h | ENISA early warning |
| 72 h | ENISA notification |
| 14 d | ENISA final report |

Penalty: up to EUR 15 M or 2.5 % of worldwide turnover.

When a dependency advisory drops, developers spend hours answering "are we even
affected?" — most alerts cover code paths the product never calls. T-24 automates
that triage in a reproducible, auditable way and, when a finding is confirmed
affected and actively exploited, drafts the required ENISA reports automatically.

---

## 1. Verified Advisory Facts

> Source: GitHub Advisory Database (CC-BY-4.0). Used in demo_product/.

| CVE | GHSA | Package | Installed | Affected range | Fixed | Vulnerable symbol | Expected verdict |

| CVE-2020-14343 | GHSA-8q59-q68h-6hv4 | PyYAML | 5.3.1 | <5.4 | 5.4 | `full_load`, `FullLoader` | AFFECTED |
| CVE-2023-50447 | GHSA-2jpm-f686-3f3r | Pillow | 9.5.0 | <10.1.0 | 10.1.0 | `PIL.ImageMath.eval` | NOT_AFFECTED (not in execute path) |
| CVE-2024-22195 | GHSA-g3fm-fvfm-84f7 | Jinja2 | 3.1.2 | <3.1.3 | 3.1.3 | `xmlattr` | NOT_AFFECTED (not in execute path) |
| CVE-2023-32681 | GHSA-hcpj-qdhc-mh72 | requests | 2.30.0 | <2.31.0 | 2.31.0 | _(none; precondition: proxy config)_ | UNDER_INVESTIGATION |

## 3. Architecture

```
advisories/*.md
      │
      ▼
[advisory.py]  ─── LLM (watsonx / Fireworks / cached) ──► extracted symbols
      │                                                      verbatim check ✓
      ▼
[inventory.py] ─── packaging.specifiers ──► version in range? (bool)
      │
      ▼
[reach.py]     ─── Python AST (ast module) ──► call graph ──► evidence path
      │              entry points from CLI args
      ▼
[verdict.py]   ─── pure deterministic logic ──► OpenVEX status + justification
      │              LLM NEVER touches verdict
      ▼
[clock.py]     ─── datetime arithmetic ──► 24h/72h/14d deadlines (if affected+exploited)
      │
      ├──► [vex.py]    ──► out/vex.json       (OpenVEX 0.2.0)
      ├──► [report.py] ──► out/drafts/*.md    (ENISA Markdown drafts)
      └──► [cli.py]    ──► out/dossier.json   (DATA_CONTRACT shape)
```

### Key design invariants

1. **The LLM only extracts symbols.** It never sets, suggests, or overrides the verdict.
2. **Verbatim symbol check.** Every symbol returned by the LLM is dropped unless it appears
   character-for-character in the advisory text. This is a deterministic post-extraction filter.
3. **not_affected requires 100 % parse coverage.** `vulnerable_code_not_in_execute_path` is
   only emitted when `files_parsed == files_found`.
4. **Preconditions block not_affected.** Any advisory that contains a runtime precondition
   that static analysis cannot prove (e.g., proxy configuration) yields `under_investigation`.
5. **Evidence is file:line hops.** Every hop in the call graph carries a file path and line
   number; the report renderer cites them directly.

## 4. Module Specifications

### 4.1 `t24/advisory.py`

**Purpose:** Read an advisory markdown file, call the LLM, return a structured
`AdvisoryExtraction` dataclass.

**Key responsibilities:**
- Load advisory text from `advisories/<CVE>.md`
- Build a prompt asking the LLM for: package, affected_range, fixed_version,
  symbols (list), preconditions (list)
- Post-extraction: drop any symbol not found verbatim in the advisory text
  (case-sensitive substring check)
- Cache result to `cache/<CVE>.json`; load from cache if present (enables offline demo)
- Provider selection: try watsonx.ai (ibm-granite/granite-3-3-8b-instruct or similar),
  fallback to Fireworks

**Dataclass:**
```python
@dataclass
class AdvisoryExtraction:
    cve: str
    package: str
    affected_range: str
    fixed_version: str
    symbols: list[str]          # verbatim-checked
    preconditions: list[str]    # e.g. ["proxies must be configured"]
    advisory_source: str        # URL from SOURCE line in markdown
    raw_advisory_text: str      # kept for evidence citation
```

**Constraints:** < 300 lines. No network calls in tests (use cache fixtures).

    affected_range: str

```

**Purpose:** Build a Python AST import+call graph over a project directory and
determine whether a set of vulnerable symbols is reachable from declared entry points.

**Key responsibilities:**
- Walk `*.py` files under the product directory
- Parse each file with `ast.parse`; record parse failures
- Build an import map: `module_alias → real_module` handling:
  - `import yaml` → `yaml`
  - `import yaml as y` → maps `y` → `yaml`
  - `from yaml import full_load` → `full_load` in local scope
  - `from yaml import full_load as fl` → maps `fl` → `yaml.full_load`
  - Attribute chains: `yaml.full_load(...)` resolves via import map
- Build a call graph: function → set of (callee_name, file, line)
- BFS/DFS from entry points to find evidence path to each vulnerable symbol

    file: str
    line: int
    function: str
    call: str

@dataclass
class ReachResult:
    symbol: str
    reachable: bool
    evidence: list[EvidenceHop]
    files_found: int
    files_parsed: int
```

### 4.4 `t24/verdict.py`

**Purpose:** Apply deterministic verdict logic. The LLM never touches this.

**Decision tree (exact):**

```
if not version_check.in_range:
    → status=not_affected, justification=vulnerable_code_not_present

elif version_check.in_range AND symbols extracted AND any symbol reachable:
    → status=affected, justification=null, evidence=<hop list>

elif version_check.in_range AND symbols extracted
     AND none reachable AND coverage==100% AND no preconditions:

elif version_check.in_range AND preconditions exist (unprovable statically):
    → status=under_investigation

else:  # no symbols named, or parse failures, or partial coverage
    → status=under_investigation
```

    status: Literal["affected", "not_affected", "under_investigation", "fixed"]
    justification: str | None
    evidence: list[EvidenceHop]
    reason: str           # human-readable one-liner
```

**Constraints:** Zero LLM calls. Pure Python logic. < 300 lines.

### 4.5 `t24/clock.py`

**Purpose:** Compute CRA Article 14 report deadlines and return structured clock data.

**Key responsibilities:**
- Accept `aware_at: datetime` (ISO 8601, timezone-aware)
- Compute:
  - `early_warning_due = aware_at + 24h`
  - `notification_due = aware_at + 72h`
  - `final_report_due = aware_at + 14d`
- Return `CRAClock` dataclass
- Only invoked when finding is `affected` AND `--actively-exploited` flag is set

**Dataclass:**
```python
@dataclass
class CRAClock:
    cve: str
    aware_at: datetime
    early_warning_due: datetime
    notification_due: datetime
    final_report_due: datetime
```

**Constraints:** stdlib `datetime` only. No network.

**Purpose:** Serialize findings to OpenVEX 0.2.0 JSON format.

**Key responsibilities:**
- Build an OpenVEX document with `@context`, `@id`, `timestamp`,

**Purpose:** Render ENISA early warning and notification drafts as Markdown.

**Key responsibilities:**

- Template for notification (Art. 14 §2): adds impact assessment,
  actions taken, cross-references
- Every factual claim cites `file:line` or an advisory line number
- Write to `out/drafts/early_warning_<CVE>.md` and `out/drafts/notification_<CVE>.md`

### 4.8 `t24/cli.py` + `t24/__main__.py`

**Purpose:** Typer-based CLI that wires all modules together and writes outputs.

**CLI signature:**
```
t24 scan \
  --product <path>          # path to product directory
  --advisories <path>       # path to advisories directory (default: ./advisories)
  --entry-points <list>     # comma-separated module:function or file:function
  --actively-exploited <CVE>=<ISO8601>  # can repeat; sets aware_at for clock
  --out <path>              # output directory (default: ./out)

**Output contract:** writes `out/vex.json` and `out/dossier.json` per

`python -m t24` works.

+> "Prove whether you're affected before the CRA clock runs out."
+> IBM Bob 2.0 Hackathon — Theme: Improve a developer workflow

+---
+
+## 0. Problem and Goal
+
+Since 11 Sep 2026, EU Cyber Resilience Act Article 14 requires:
+
+| Deadline | Action |
+|----------|--------|
+| 24 h | ENISA early warning |
+| 72 h | ENISA notification |
+| 14 d | ENISA final report |
+
+Penalty: up to EUR 15 M or 2.5 % of worldwide turnover.
+
+When a dependency advisory drops, developers spend hours answering "are we even
+affected?" — most alerts cover code paths the product never calls. T-24 automates
+that triage in a reproducible, auditable way and, when a finding is confirmed
+affected and actively exploited, drafts the required ENISA reports automatically.

+## 3. Architecture
+
+```
+advisories/*.md
+      │
+      ▼
+[advisory.py]  ─── LLM (watsonx / Fireworks / cached) ──► extracted symbols
+      │                                                      verbatim check ✓
+      ▼
+[inventory.py] ─── packaging.specifiers ──► version in range? (bool)
+      │
+      ▼
+[reach.py]     ─── Python AST (ast module) ──► call graph ──► evidence path
+      │              entry points from CLI args
+      ▼
+[verdict.py]   ─── pure deterministic logic ──► OpenVEX status + justification
+      │              LLM NEVER touches verdict
+      ▼
+[clock.py]     ─── datetime arithmetic ──► 24h/72h/14d deadlines (if affected+exploited)
+      │
+      ├──► [vex.py]    ──► out/vex.json       (OpenVEX 0.2.0)
+      ├──► [report.py] ──► out/drafts/*.md    (ENISA Markdown drafts)
+      └──► [cli.py]    ──► out/dossier.json   (DATA_CONTRACT shape)
+```
+
+### Key design invariants
+
+1. **The LLM only extracts symbols.** It never sets, suggests, or overrides the verdict.
+2. **Verbatim symbol check.** Every symbol returned by the LLM is dropped unless it appears
+   character-for-character in the advisory text. This is a deterministic post-extraction filter.
+3. **not_affected requires 100 % parse coverage.** `vulnerable_code_not_in_execute_path` is
+   only emitted when `files_parsed == files_found`.
+4. **Preconditions block not_affected.** Any advisory that contains a runtime precondition
+   that static analysis cannot prove (e.g., proxy configuration) yields `under_investigation`.
+5. **Evidence is file:line hops.** Every hop in the call graph carries a file path and line
+   number; the report renderer cites them directly.

+## 4. Module Specifications
+
+### 4.1 `t24/advisory.py`
+
+**Purpose:** Read an advisory markdown file, call the LLM, return a structured
+`AdvisoryExtraction` dataclass.
+
+**Key responsibilities:**
+- Load advisory text from `advisories/<CVE>.md`
+- Build a prompt asking the LLM for: package, affected_range, fixed_version,
+  symbols (list), preconditions (list)
+- Post-extraction: drop any symbol not found verbatim in the advisory text
+  (case-sensitive substring check)
+- Cache result to `cache/<CVE>.json`; load from cache if present (enables offline demo)
+- Provider selection: try watsonx.ai (ibm-granite/granite-3-3-8b-instruct or similar),
+  fallback to Fireworks
+
+**Dataclass:**
+```python
+@dataclass
+class AdvisoryExtraction:
+    cve: str
+    package: str
+    affected_range: str
+    fixed_version: str
+    symbols: list[str]          # verbatim-checked
+    preconditions: list[str]    # e.g. ["proxies must be configured"]
+    advisory_source: str        # URL from SOURCE line in markdown
+    raw_advisory_text: str      # kept for evidence citation
+```
+
+**Constraints:** < 300 lines. No network calls in tests (use cache fixtures).
+
+---
+
+### 4.2 `t24/inventory.py`
+
+**Purpose:** Parse `requirements.txt`, resolve installed versions, check each
+package version against the extracted affected range.
+
+**Key responsibilities:**
+- Parse `requirements.txt` with `packaging.requirements`
+- Normalize package names (PEP 503 canonical form)
+- Use `packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet` to test membership
+- Return `VersionCheck` dataclass per package
+
+**Dataclass:**
+```python
+@dataclass
+class VersionCheck:
+    package: str
+    installed: str
+    affected_range: str
+    in_range: bool
+```
+
+**Constraints:** Pure stdlib + `packaging`. No network.

+
+### 4.3 `t24/reach.py`
+
+**Purpose:** Build a Python AST import+call graph over a project directory and
+determine whether a set of vulnerable symbols is reachable from declared entry points.
+
+**Key responsibilities:**
+- Walk `*.py` files under the product directory
+- Parse each file with `ast.parse`; record parse failures
+- Build an import map: `module_alias → real_module` handling:
+  - `import yaml` → `yaml`
+  - `import yaml as y` → maps `y` → `yaml`
+  - `from yaml import full_load` → `full_load` in local scope
+  - `from yaml import full_load as fl` → maps `fl` → `yaml.full_load`
+  - Attribute chains: `yaml.full_load(...)` resolves via import map
+- Build a call graph: function → set of (callee_name, file, line)
+- BFS/DFS from entry points to find evidence path to each vulnerable symbol
+- Track `files_found` and `files_parsed` for coverage
+
+**Dataclass:**
+```python
+@dataclass
+class EvidenceHop:
+    file: str
+    line: int
+    function: str
+    call: str
+
+@dataclass
+class ReachResult:
+    symbol: str
+    reachable: bool
+    evidence: list[EvidenceHop]
+    files_found: int
+    files_parsed: int
+```
+
+**Constraints:** Uses only `ast` (stdlib). No network. < 300 lines.
+
+---
+
+### 4.4 `t24/verdict.py`
+
+**Purpose:** Apply deterministic verdict logic. The LLM never touches this.
+
+**Decision tree (exact):**
+
+```
+if not version_check.in_range:
+    → status=not_affected, justification=vulnerable_code_not_present
+
+elif version_check.in_range AND symbols extracted AND any symbol reachable:
+    → status=affected, justification=null, evidence=<hop list>
+
+elif version_check.in_range AND symbols extracted
+     AND none reachable AND coverage==100% AND no preconditions:
+    → status=not_affected, justification=vulnerable_code_not_in_execute_path
+
+elif version_check.in_range AND preconditions exist (unprovable statically):
+    → status=under_investigation
+
+else:  # no symbols named, or parse failures, or partial coverage
+    → status=under_investigation
+```
+
+**Output:**
+```python
+@dataclass
+class VerdictResult:
+    cve: str
+    status: Literal["affected", "not_affected", "under_investigation", "fixed"]
+    justification: str | None
+    evidence: list[EvidenceHop]
+    reason: str           # human-readable one-liner
+```
+
+**Constraints:** Zero LLM calls. Pure Python logic. < 300 lines.
+

+  - `final_report_due = aware_at + 14d`
+- Return `CRAClock` dataclass

+**Constraints:** No LLM calls in rendering. Templates use Python f-strings or
+`string.Template`. < 300 lines.
+
+---
+
+### 4.8 `t24/cli.py` + `t24/__main__.py`
+
+**Purpose:** Typer-based CLI that wires all modules together and writes outputs.
+
+**CLI signature:**
+```
+t24 scan \
+  --product <path>          # path to product directory
+  --advisories <path>       # path to advisories directory (default: ./advisories)
+  --entry-points <list>     # comma-separated module:function or file:function
+  --actively-exploited <CVE>=<ISO8601>  # can repeat; sets aware_at for clock
+  --out <path>              # output directory (default: ./out)
+  --no-cache                # bypass LLM cache
+```
+
+**Output contract:** writes `out/vex.json` and `out/dossier.json` per
+`docs/DATA_CONTRACT.md`, and `out/drafts/*.md` when due.
+
+**`__main__.py`:** single line — `from t24.cli import app; app()` so
+`python -m t24` works.
+
+---
+
+## 5. Demo Product
+
+`demo_product/app.py` — a minimal Flask label-printer service:
+
+| Route | Code | Reason for expected verdict |
+|-------|------|----------------------------|
+| `POST /upload-config` | `yaml.full_load(request.data)` | Calls vulnerable symbol directly |
+| `POST /thumbnail` | `Image.open(...).thumbnail(...)` | Uses Pillow but not ImageMath.eval |
+| `GET /label/<id>` | `render_template(...)` | Uses Jinja2 but not xmlattr filter |
+| `GET /fetch-label` | `requests.get(url)` | No proxy config; precondition unprovable |
+
+`demo_product/requirements.txt`:
+```
+Flask==2.3.0
+PyYAML==5.3.1
+Pillow==9.5.0
+Jinja2==3.1.2
+requests==2.30.0
+```
+
+Entry point for reachability: `demo_product/app.py`
+
+---
+
+## 6. Advisory Files
+
+Each file in `advisories/` is Markdown with at minimum:
+
+```markdown
+# <CVE> — <Title>
+
+SOURCE: <GitHub Advisory Database URL>
+
+## Summary
+...advisory text verbatim or paraphrased...
+
+## Affected Versions
+...
+
+## Vulnerable Symbols
+...
+```

+The `SOURCE:` line is parsed by `advisory.py` to populate `advisory_source`.

+---

+### Custom Mode — `t24-mode`
